"The Hague" - Artificial colours of flavors, the so-called E-numbers, deceive consumers and lead to unnecessary risks to health. That's what the Consumers' Association said yesterday. The interest organisation has mapped out the dangers of additives to food, such as the risk of cancer. "They often mask the lack of colour, smell or taste of food. They mislead the consumer, according to the association. Even though the substances are basically safe, various additives know certain health risks, such as allergic reactions. Hyperactivity in children can be the result of eating artificial dyes like tartrazine (E102) and erythrosine (E127). "Some artificial colors of flavors are not entirely free from the suspicion of causing or promoting cancer." Examples are the colorants E110, E123, E133, the antioxidants E320 and E321, the colouring agent E407.

The Dutch cook fastest from all over the world ROTTERDAM The Dutch want to eat fast: they cook fastest worldwide and eat most of the Western Europeans take away meals. This and other cuisine habits are evident from an international study of furniture group Ikea among 14,000 people in 27 countries. The Dutch have a meal together in an average of 40 minutes, while the rest of the world spends an hour on it. Most of the time it is women who cook. In particular, Japanese people have a role-confirming role, only four percent of the men are behind the stove. In addition, the Dutch men are still involved: in over twenty percent of the households the man cooks. Furthermore, the research gives insight into remarkable cuisine habits. 33 percent of the Finns regularly prepare a meal naked or only dressed underwear.

Food in shops and restaurants often poorly preserved DEN HAAG In one on the three shops, restaurants and health care institutions a lot of food is stored at the wrong temperature. The British government is arguing about smoking ban in pub Dividement in British Cabinet LONDON The British government is arguing about the introduction of a smoking ban in pubs and bars. Dividement among ministers has led to a delay in a bill that should have been dealt with yesterday. According to some party members, the disagreement points out that Prime Minister Blair is losing his influence, according to the newspaper The Times. After ministers could not agree on Monday, Minister of Health Patricia Hewitt called with her colleagues. Afterwards she thought an agreement had been reached. Pubs serving food would get a complete smoking ban. In the other bars, however, customers would only be allowed to smoke in ' closed rooms. Ministers John Reid (Defensie) and his associate Jack Straw (Buitenland Affairs) didn't support the compromise. Reid called on the original plans, which he himself as Minister of Health. There would be a full smoking ban for the dining places, but other pubs themselves should be given the choice to not to smoke.

Beef from the Netherlands is almost 100 percent safe. Since 1989 a large number of measures have been taken to prevent the contamination of beef from entering the food chain. Even before slaughter all bovine animals are subjected to a test on mad cow disease. In Europe cattle aged 30 months and older are tested on bse during slaughter. Slaughterhouses have to remove the risk material - such as spine and skull - from the carcass. That offal can no longer be fed as animal meal to cattle. This happened until halfway through the year 90, which allowed bse to spread. The EU rules followed the bse crisis in Great Britain. More than 150 people were infected with Creutzfeldt-Jakob by eating bse meat. The severe measures have had an effect in the EU.

The cruise ship of P & O Cruises with a number of sick passengers on board has made a stopover in Aruba and has continued its 14-day journey in the Caribbean. Of the more than 1,800 passengers of the Oceana there are 116 stomach and bowel complaints. Also four crew members are sick. According to a spokesperson of P& O it is probably a variant of the Norwalk virus. The Norwalk virus has struck three other cruise ships in recent weeks: the Amsterdam of Holland America Line, the Fascination of Camival Cruise Lines and the Magic of Disney Cruise Line. In total, a thousand passengers were ill. The ships are thoroughly cleaned. The Norwalk virus is a persistent virus that causes nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting and abdominal cramps. From time to time there is a large outbreak - in 1993 a large 200 people became sick by eating infected oysters. The virus occurs worldwide but in America is the main cause for food poisoning.

Prey is hunting wolf boss KRYINGLOOP On an island in the state of Michigan, wolves and American mooses are closely watched by biologists. They have been studying the balance between hunters and prey for 44 years. The moose benefit from the mild winter this year. They have enough to eat and are strong enough to keep the wolves away. Their number rose from 900 to 1100. Of the wolves there are only 7 left, two less than last year.

The British are going to investigate the extent of the threat posed by a very unpleasant type of ladybird that has landed in Europe in an inexplicable way. The animals, of the originally Asian species Harmonia axyridis (also known as Harlequin Ladybird), are particularly voracious. In times of food scarcity, they are even cannibalistic and eat other kinds of ladybirds. How the Asian gluttons exactly landed in Great Britain, France, Belgium and the Netherlands, is not clear. They may come from the US, where they are often used in the fight against insects on plants. Via consignments of fruit they would have ended up in Europe.

Yom Kippur Yom Kippur is the most holy day of the Jewish year. On October 12th, God decides on the fate of the people in the coming year. The Jews confess their own and common sins. On Yom Kippur it is forbidden to eat and drink, to wash and to have sexual association. Also, the Orthodox Jew may not wear leather shoes. Thus he shows that he respects the holiness of the earth. Yom Kippur's celebration is solemn, but not gloomy, because the new year gives opportunities to do everything better.

The Dutchman finds himself fit Amsterdam - Over 90 percent of the Dutch people call themselves fit. This is shown by a poll of the magazine Body+Mind. Almost all research participants, 500 people aged 12 years and older, think they have a reasonable to good condition. More than 50 percent of the respondents say to exercise or otherwise move (biking, hiking). More than 20 percent regularly visit a fitness club and 10 percent plan to go to the gym this year. Almost 15 percent do not at all. The food industry, the food industry, the catering industry, the health insurers, the sports organizations and the ministries of Public Health and Education announced together last month a plan to fight overweight. The reason was the increase in (severe) overweight in the Netherlands, a result of unhealthy eating and low movement.

"Warm-up effect only" Electromagnetic fields (also called radiation) are derived from devices in our environment, such as mobile phones, cell towers, radar, DECT phones and wireless computer networks. Also our electricity grid with all connected devices emits electromagnetic fields in low frequency. A microwave, for example, works on electromagnetic fields, but these do not come out. Science has been discussing the effects of this radiation on humans, plants and animals for years. The Health Council considers that until now only proven that the fields give a warming effect. This can be seen in the microwave, which warms us up in no time. According to the Health Council, however, the warming effect in the head when calling with a mobile phone is negligiblely small. But also other, so-called non-thermal effects, such as dizziness and nausea, are attributed to electromagnetic fields in some investigations.

Exhilarating spiders Chilean scientists are working on the development of a pill that can remedy impotence and at the same time works as a contraceptive pill for the man. They have found these properties in the sometimes deadly poison of the black widow. The female of this spider has the habit of eating her partner after mating. The poison that the spider produces can, among other things, stiffen muscles. Researchers from the Universiteit La Frontera in Temuco, in southern Chile, have spent seven years studying the properties of the poison of the black widow. In November, they discovered by chance that it contains an ingredient that the man cannot lend an erection, but also makes his sperm sterile without causing harmful side effects.

New medicine against Alzheimer's DEMENTIE With the medicine memantine (brand name: Ebixa), the pharmaceutical company Lundbeck hopes to introduce a new approach to Alzheimer's disease. It counteracts the disturbed signal transmission in Alzheimer's patients. This interference is caused by an increased concentration of glutamate in the nerve cell. Memantine is the first approved medicine for moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease worldwide. Research shows that it improves cognitive functions (speech, understanding, alertness) in these patients. Also in the area of daily activities (such as eating, walking, going to the toilet) and quality of life.

Urker men die more often of heart disease Urk - Urk men die more often of cardiovascular disease than the rest of the Dutch men. Mortality was 36 percent higher between 1985 and 1997. In 1985 there were over 11,000 Urkers and at the end of 1997 there were 15.000. At that time, 487 men died, of whom 210 were heart disease. In the deceased women were 141 out of 370. For the "Overdiction mortality" there are three possible explanations. Many men are fishermen. In all age groups they smoke more often and eat more food with saturated fat and cholesterol. As a result they are often thicker than average and suffer more from high blood pressure and hypercholesterolemia.

NET AS ZONE AS MEAT Vegetarian food can be as healthy as a menu with meat, says Patricia Schutte of the Food Centre in The Hague. Meat contains iron and vitamin B 12, substances necessary for the production of red blood cells. However, iron is also contained in pulses, nuts, eggs and soy products. B vitamins are found in dairy products such as milk, yoghurt or eggs. Meat substitutes such as Tivall, which is made from soya beans, and Quorn (a vegetable protein) contain B-12 one iron. Newcomer Valess, made from lean milk and seaweed, contains no iron. For an adult state 100 grams of meat or fish equal to 100 grams of tofu, 75 grams of prepared legumes, 40 grams of nuts, 100 grams of meat substitute or two eggs.

Creutzfeldt Jakob Creutzfeldt Jakob is a disease that occurs in three variants. A prion (protein) reproduces and affects the brain so slowly but irrevocably. This usually leads to death within a year. No evidence has yet been found for its origin, only strong indications. The first species, the classic, occurs without obvious cause. This species occurs among about one million people and therefore also in the Netherlands. The second species is genetically determined. The third species is caused by contamination, for example by eating meat, but also by infected instruments, heart and brain transplants and injecting with human growth hormones.

There are two types of sweat glands. The apocrine glands are located under the armpits. They secrete a substance that - however uncomfortable we may find this smell - libido-enhancing works. The eccriene glands are located all over the body. These get the signal of the nerves to separate moisture when the body temperature rises. This way, a healthy body temperature is maintained. Some people perspirate already with low exertion, while others hardly sweat. In them, the sweat glands secrete so little fluid that it is already evaporated, before a layer of moisture can form on the skin. Transpiration is often a result of emotion. Also eating spicy dishes can make us sweat. Furthermore, there are certain medicines that cause excessive sweating.

The egg from which the condor was born was placed by the biologists in a nest that was used by two females at the same time. Another delay of polar travellers From one of our reporters ROTTERDAM The Arctic expedition Pole Track continues to slow down. The Dutchman Mare Cornelissen and his companions Doug Stoup and Petter Nyquist, who want to map the effects of climate change in the Arctic, are not allowed by the Russian authorities to leave the airport of Khatanga to start their journey. The polar passengers left the Netherlands on February 16th and would enter the ice a week later. All sorts of formalities caused immediate delay, but last weekend the expedition seemed to be able to start. At the moment the helicopter wanted to take off to take off the men, the border surveillance still threw soot into the food. What the reason for the new hold-up is unclear. Cerpolex, the company that accompanies the expedition, suspects that a Russian competitor is behind the setback. Pole Track's team will have to make concessions in any case.

Bacterie cleans raw coal from our reporters Washington - Coal energy can be cleaner and more efficient. American researchers have grown coal-eating bacteria that remove harmful substances for combustion from the coal mass. Crude coal is contaminated with sulphur and nitrogen. In combustion, these substances are released: they cause acid rain, among others. Coal also often contains high concentrations of heavy metals. For many years, researchers have been looking for a method to remove these harmful substances from the raw coal. Scheists from the US Department of Energy have now grown a bacterium, which separates sulphur, nitrogen and heavy metals from the coal. Americans have been using a bacterium strain that lives in geysers for their research. As a result, the species was already used to high temperatures. Gradually, the researches added more coal to the food of the strain. After a number of generations of bacteria that survived on raw coal. They also proved to be resistant to the high temperatures produced during the refining process.

Schools dead by food poisoning MANILLA At least 27 pupils from a Filipino primary school died by food poisoning after eating caramelized cassava root in the morning break. More than 100 pupils are still in four different hospitals. It is taken into account that the number of deaths will occur. In the school panic broke out when hundreds of pupils started to vomit and experienced severe stomach cramps. Agitated parents brought their sick children to hospitals in the remote city of Mabini on the island of Bohol. Dead children were lying, covered in white sheets, in the trunk of a truck. The roots of the cassava plant are rich in proteins, minerals and vitamins, but also contain the poisonous blue acid. Two tubers may already contain a fatal dose if the preparation is not good. A doctor in a hospital where47 patients were admitted, said the cake tasted bitter and that the children had severe stomach pains after two bites.

High blood pressure is becoming too high a blood pressure in 2025. They make their predictions in the British medical journal The Lancet, which appears Saturday. An excessive blood pressure occurs when the pressure in the blood vessels is too high. The heart must pump hard to get the blood through the vessels. It is a dangerous condition. People can suffer from it for years without them being aware of it. Eventually, the body gets damaged to the heart, the brain, kidneys and/or legs. People can get a heart attack, stroke or kidney failure. Also, they can hardly walk anymore because the blood supply to their legs is disturbed. Older people, too fat people and people with an unhealthy lifestyle are at increased risk. Experts already expect the hypertension, or high blood pressure, an increasing problem. The population is ageing, people are eating more often unhealthy and are all risk of being exposed to high blood pressure.

Oldest man in the world 112 years Tiana - The oldest man in the world, the Italian shepherd Antonio Todde, became 112 years old yesterday. He was recognized as the oldest man in the world on 9 December, a few days after the death of 111-year-old American Benjamin Holcomb. Todde, who was born in the year when the Eiffel Tower was opened, had stayed home to his house in the village of Tiana on Sardinia on Sunday. He had already celebrated with his family. He says that he has become so old every day by eating a piece of meat and cheese and drinking a nice glass of wine. He thinks he can become 120 or 130 years old. The oldest resident of the Netherlands is the 113-year-old Catharina Angenieta of DamGroeneveld from Leiden. The oldest Dutch man is Jan Pieter Bos (109) from Rotterdam.

Cats are more difficult than dogs Cats are a lot more difficult than dogs. They are territorial animals that prefer to stay in their own environment and adapt to a new setting. Moreover, a cat is difficult to read about what he thinks of something. That's mainly because a cat sleeps 16 hours a day. Many cats give the impression that they have enough to themselves, but they also need incentives. Thus, a cat gets away with a clean cat box and enough to eat, but he doesn't like it. Cats are not only territorial, but also need company. Most cats are therefore crazy about toys. That's why you have to deal with them wisely, because cats are sometimes just children. If you give them a new toy and let them pick it out themselves, they'll be there after a month. But if you take the toy and play with it again, it'll take longer. Cats also find it important that their territory is varied.

The results of this study, led by Professor Luc van Gaal of the University Hospital in Antwerp, have been published in The Lancet. For one year 1507 too thick subjects were given 20 or 5 milligrams rimonabant or a placebo daily. After one year the weight loss in those who received the high dose was highest, on average 6.6 kilos. In the five milligrams group the loss was 3.4 kilos and in the placebo group 1.8 kilos. In those who received 20 milligrams lost three-quarters five percent of his body weight and over one third lost 10 percent. Rimonabant does not only result in weight loss but also affects the risk factors for heart and vascular diseases. The values for HDL cholesterol, triglycerides and insulin resistance were much better for the 20 milligrams group than for the participants who swallowed a placebo. The conclusion of Van Gaal is that rimonabant is true to its promise.

Embryo of dinosaur revealed From our editorial abroad JOHANNESBURG South African scientists have revealed the 190 million-year-old embryo of a Massospondylus dinosaur. It is about the oldest embryo ever found. A sketch artist made an artistic impression on the skeleton of the curled unborn creature. It has four legs, a short tail and a relatively large head. Economics grew by 3.9 percent of our reporters Voorburg - The Dutch economy has grown by 3.9 percent over the past year. This was the same as in 1999. It was the fourth consecutive year with a growth of around 4 percent, according to the Central Bureau of Statistics. The price level of gross domestic product (GDP) increased by 3.2 percent over the past year. Investment growth fell from 6.5 percent in 1999 to 4.0 percent in 2000. Obsessed with weight, body and size In the Netherlands, about 40,000 women have a severe eating disorder. Men with an eating disorder form a very small minority. People with an eating disorder are obsessed with everything that has to do with food, weight and body size. Almost all people with an eating disorder think that their body looks different than in reality. They consider themselves mud fat, while they can be skinny. Moreover, they have a negative self-image. Experience shows that behind these delusions often other problems, such as sexual abuse or bullying at school. An eating disorder can manifest itself in three ways: 1. Patients with anorexia nervosa have an irresistible urge to fall off. 2. Patients with bulimia nervosa have eating problems in which they can eliminate large amounts (calorious) of food and then break out again (compensation behaviour).

Sex taboo for UN peace-power From our correspondent Cape Town - Peacekeepers for the Democratic Republic of Congo are no longer allowed to have sex with local women. The United Nations hopes to prevent new sexual scandals in Congo. The so-called non-fraternization clause comes directly from UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan. At the beginning of this year, a committee of inquiry on sexual abuse by UN military forces in the northeast of Congo reported. In exchange for sex, girls received food or money from foreign troops. The committee called for tough measures. The 12,000 blue helmets from among others Morocco, Nepal, South Africa and Uruguay, in the new provision, are no longer allowed to go out in the evening. The troops do get wider opportunities for relaxation within the barracks) and outside Congo. The UN has already faced more complaints about alleged sexual abuse in Africa. Three years ago, organizations in Western Africa reported that workers from humanitarian organizations in SiÃrra Leone and soldiers of the UN peace-power in the country demanded that sexual services in that have been conducted by women.

Emergency fund to deal with abuses in nursing homes From our political editors The Hague - The Cabinet puts 10 million euros in an emergency fund to combat abuses in nursing homes. The money is intended for a flying brigade of doctors and managers who are going to help the poor nursing homes solve the worst abuses. That is what Secretary of State Ross (Folks Health) said yesterday in the Second Chamber during a debate on nursing care. In many institutions care is far below the standard. Patients sometimes get too little food and drink. Also older people are often in bed too long. The State Secretary has already announced an investigation into the causes of the abuses. That must be done before the summer. Ross is willing to make extra money available if it turns out that lack of money causes the problems. By the way, Ross expects that most problems are solved by a better management of the nursing homes.

Bananas with extinction threats London / Montpellier - The banana threatens to die out. Scientists in the southern French Montpellier have informed the British science magazine the New Scientist that without large scale intervention there will probably be no edible bananas in ten years' time. Two fungal diseases, one called Panama and the other called Black Sigatoka, eradicate the banana as we know it and eat it. Normally, as in the case of potato diseases, resistant variants can be grown. But that is precisely the problem with the conventional banana, says Emile Frison of the International Network for the Improvement of Banana and Pisang (INIBAP). Frison, who works in Montpellier, says in the New Scientist, that it is extremely difficult to grow a resistant banana. The banana itself is a sterile mutant of an inedible wild banana plant, not planted.

Ross gives 40 million extra to nursing homes From our political editors DEN HAAG Nursing homes with patients who need extra care can claim extra money in 2006. State Secretary Ross (Volksgezondheid) has allocated 40 million euros for this. Institutions that want to make use of the money must prioritize the care of their patients. For example, nursing homes with many heavily in need clients such as dementias, elderly and disabled people - make more chance of extra money. Nursing homes have been complaining for years that the existing rates are insufficient to take care of the increasingly severe patients. Yesterday, the State Secretary agreed with a series of measures to improve nursing home care. Ross came up with proposals in response to the report of topman Hans Kennedie of hotel chain Golden Tulip. At Ross' request he explained the nursing sector. The State Secretary now agrees with his recommendations. Kennedie also argued this month for the introduction of a star system for nursing homes.

This time, there is a typical summer problem for pet owners: fleas! Where do they come from and how do you get off? It gets warmer again, the days longer; the summer comes. Do you have mammals as pets? Then beware of fleas. Through the fleas I even get people without pets in my practice every summer. They want an anti-flying spray, because they still have fleas in their house. How can that? Adult fleas live on dogs and cats. During their adult life the females lay eggs on the ground. Other than lice, which cling their eggs (nets) to the fleece, let their eggs fall out of it. So wherever our pets run, hundreds of eggs fall on the ground per fleas do not come out of these eggs on the ground. From these eggs, for example, they hide behind plinting or ringing from a wooden floor. There they feed on house dust and within a few weeks they come out of these adult fleas. So everywhere where our pets are susceptible, they can't find their eggs on the ground.

The attraction of low-wage Insight The attraction of China, which wants to get hold of half of the world textile market, is in the low wages. An hour's work on the sewing machine costs 92 dollars cents versus 1.20 dollars in Thailand, 1.70 dollars in Mexico and 21.80 dollars in the United States, says a study by Goldman Sachs. Only India is cheaper. The wages are low because China does not have difficult unions: the state trade union has Tiet continuing its productionâat the top of the statutes. Also a large surplus of millions of labour in the countryside makes labor cheap. Chinese workers living in dormitories of the factory, eat in joint factory canteens and are therefore available 24 hours a day for shift services. The workers are young, obedient ex-farmers who find the work in the factory a light and well-paid job. The size of factories 20,000 workers are no exception - makes super fast delivery of giant orders possible. The majority of raw materials are widely available in China, and are already frightening cheap. The factories have established the best machinery in China, where they are not able to compete with regional companies.

The Argentine government, partly free Noodplan government, must prevent social crisis by our correspondent Anke Welten Buenos Aires - Two days later than planned, Minister Jorge Remes Lenicov of economic affairs announced an economic emergency plan last night. He confirmed reports that were already in the newspapers in the morning: the Argentines can now have salaries transferred to bank accounts. Part of the bank accounts that had been frozen since early December last year are also confirmed: all bank debts are converted into dollars today and tomorrow the banks are closed at a value of 1 peso on 1 dollar and bank balances at a price of 1.40 peso. The market value of the peso is about 50 dollar. These measures will cost the Argentine state thirty billion dollar. Unclear where that amount is to come from. Today and tomorrow the banks are closed again.

City life China is very unhealthy Shanghai - Who lives in China in a large city, plays with his life. The average life expectancy for well-educated city dwellers is 58 years, 14 years shorter than the average life span at national level. In Shanghai and Guangzhou that percentage is 73. The mortality rate at the Chinese elite is fastest. The main reasons for this are: too little attention to health, lack of movement and too much tension. The health problems at the higher and middle-aged employees are so great that the Red Cross defines good health in a study as disease. Sunshine can protect against MS London - Sunshine can protect people from the nervous disease multiple sclerosis. This is shown by studies from the University of EastAnglia. The studies have spread over 30 countries from the equator to the polar regions. According to researcher Graham Bentham was already known that people in northern regions have a significantly greater chance of MS than people living around the equator. The key appears to be vitamin D. According to Bentham sunlight can suppress the immune system, but it also has a protective effect through the production of vitamin D. During the research it appeared that people living on the Norwegian coast and in Iceland have less MS than residents of other areas with the same climate. Here too, the statement is sought in vitamin D. This substance is in fish such as salmon and herring, which are eaten there a lot. A similar story applies to high blood pressure and strokes. Those quails are much less common to the equator than in the north. Here too vitamin D, which is produced by sunlight, responsible for the difference.

Often after 10 years of suffering from breast cancer By Peter Hofland Hamburg - Women who have had breast cancer, often years after their healing still have severe physical and emotional complaints. Two of the three women who were under 50 years of age when they had breast cancer, still struggled ten years after treatment with the nawees. This is shown by a study of the Integral Cancer Centre South (IKZ) in Eindhoven among 250 women. The results are presented at a congress in Hamburg. One in ten women in the Netherlands get breast cancer. After five years, on average 80 percent of patients are cured. However, this does not mean that the problems are over. Pain on the arm and fatigue are common symptoms. One in ten women still struggle with emotional problems after ten years. Also problems at work (20 percent), financial difficulties (17 percent) and sexual problems (34 percent) are mentioned. The pain in the arm is the result of removing the lymph glands, the prolonged fatigue is caused by chemotherapy.

Economics is falling by Van een onze verslagverbouwderen " Rotterdam-The Dutch economy is growing. As consumption is no longer declining and exports are increasing, growth in the first quarter of this year reached 4.7 percent, according to the Central Bureau for Statistics (CBS). The record growth from 1998 is in sight. It also seemed that the lower consumption growth of the end of 1999 would continue. In that year, the consumer growth went back from 4.4 to 3.3 percent. However, consumption grew in the first three months of 2000 as much as 4.6 percent compared to the first quarter of last year, so CBS also announced yesterday. In this way, the Dutch consumer defies old economic laws, because consumption and other forces such as exports and investment have traditionally changed as a motor of the economy. The recovery in Europe leads to an increasing demand for Dutch export products, and at the same time the return of the consumption drive to record levels. Only in the first quarter of 1984 and 1998 the production growth in the Netherlands was higher than the present 4.6 percent. It is historically remarkable that the growth is changing again as a motor of the Dutch economy.

Wall Street and Nasdaq opened lower to find the way up no longer. The Dow Jones finally recorded a loss of 0.59 percent on 10487 points, while the high-tech exchange Nasdaq presented a minus 0.74 percent on 2078 points. It was the index producer prices that sooted into the food. Before opening the markets it was known that in October the index showed a plus 1.7 percent, the strongest increase since 1990. Expected a plus 0.5 percent. If the producers increased their prices then the matter of time the consumer in the store also had to pay more for his product. The strong ppi-op march clearly stimulated the fear for higher inflation, after which the American central bank, the Fed, would increase interest even more than planned. And investors did not traditionally like a high interest rate, because the price of the latter's interest would be so much more favourable.

They thus benefit from the lower penalties (maximum four years) that apply in our country for such crimes. The seven arrived yesterday morning at Schiphol. Their arrival was possible because the Second Chamber recently approved the treaty, in which Morocco and the Netherlands recorded that prisoners under conditions may serve their sentences in their own country. Among them is the 44-year-old Alex van Zon, who in the summer was forced to force his transfer to the Netherlands. There are still two prisoners in a Moroccan cell waiting for a decision to sit out their further sentences.
